description: We are a student team that is made that uses hardware and software to monitor the astronauts health in space
summary:
In space, astronauts experience a plethora of health related risks due to a lack of a strong gravitational field that are crucial to be monitored. Our app addresses one of those health concerns: the detection of blood clots in the microvascular system.

It is based on the fact that by shining a laser over a wide area of skin and taking multiple captures over a short time period, the blood flow in that area can be visualized. If it is detected that blood flow has decreased, it may indicate that a blood clot is slowly forming, and thus alarm the astronauts to take preventative action.
details:
Our app compares multiple images that have laser speckle pattern on them, contrasts the differences thus allowing to determine the blood flow and micro vascular changes.

Additionally, we constructed a real-life set-up to test our idea. We built a box with cut out holes for a hand, laser and a phone camera. A dark environment provides clearer images. To diffuse the laser over an area, we used a clear plastic bag, cut in two and layered in perpendicular directions to avoid anisotropic scattering. Then, after making sure all the devices are connected to the same Wi-Fi network and properly configured, "Scan" is pressed on our app and the laser and phone camera are simultaneously switched on. After automatically saving the captures to a shared folder, the app can be used to contrast the differences in the images, thus allowing to determine the blood flow.

The main benefit of our app is that it provides an easy and cheap method to perform diagnostic check-ups for astronauts.

The app was coded in Python. For the hardware-software interface, we used Open Camera, an open source camera app, and an ESP32 microcontroller for the laser.
projectRefs: Viable seed detection using laser-speckle imaging
